question: What protective claim is made about the body such that poison does not enter it even if bitten by great serpents?
premises: A person is described as bitten by great serpents.
Poison is the agent in question.
It is claimed that poison does not enter the body in that case.
inference: Even when bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body of the person in question.
uncertainties: The reason for this protection is not stated in this verse alone.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
